item.title: Indonesia Logs More Than 43,000 Earthquakes in 2025, Death Toll Remains Low
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia experienced a high level of seismic activity throughout 2025, with more than 43,000 earthquakes recorded across the archipelago, according to the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG). Despite the high frequency of earthquakes, the human toll from seismic events remained relatively low. item.title: Fresh Year, Fresh Risk: Indonesia Stock Market Surges 1.17% in First Close of 2026
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s stock market closed its first trading session of 2026 on a strong note, with the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) jumping 101 points, or 1.17%, to finish at 8,748 on Friday, reflecting renewed risk appetite after the New Year holiday. The benchmark index moved within a range of 8,664 to 8,748 during the session. Total trading volume reached 51.15 billion shares, with turnover amounting to Rp 22.27 trillion ($1.33 billion). item.title: Explainer: What’s the Difference Between Indonesia’s Golden Visa and GCI?
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia has introduced two distinct immigration schemes — the Golden Visa and the Global Citizenship of Indonesia (GCI) — to attract investment while strengthening ties with its global diaspora. While both offer long-term residency, they differ in purpose, eligibility, and legal status. item.title: Rupiah Eases as Markets Digest FOMC Minutes and Global Tensions
item.description: Jakarta. Rupiah closed weaker against the US dollar on Friday, pressured by a mix of global monetary policy uncertainty and heightened geopolitical tensions. The Indonesian currency slipped 38 points, or 0.23%, to Rp 16,725 per dollar by the end of trading. item.title: Bali Plans Proof-of-Funds Screening for Foreign Tourists in 2026
item.description: Gianyar, Bali. The next time foreign travelers land in Bali, luggages and passports may not be the only things under scrutiny. item.title: Indonesia Enacts New Criminal Code, Regulating Cohabitation and Banning Marxism
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia has formally implemented a new Criminal Code and Criminal Procedure Law, marking the end of a legal framework rooted in Dutch colonial rule and ushering in what the government calls a more modern, rights-based justice system. The National Criminal Code (KUHP) under Law No. 1 of 2023 and the new Criminal Procedure Code (KUHAP) under Law No. 20 of 2025 took effect on Friday, replacing laws that had governed Indonesia’s criminal justice system for more than a century. item.description: Jakarta. item.title: US-Iran Tensions Flare as Trump Backs Protesters in Iran
item.description: Dubai, United Arab Emirates. US President Donald Trump and top Iranian officials exchanged dueling threats Friday as widening protests swept across parts of the Islamic Republic, escalating tensions between the countries after America bombed Iranian nuclear sites in June. item.title: Sumatra Floods Put $24 Billion in Loans at Risk, Regulator Says
item.description: Jakarta. The Financial Services Authority (OJK) estimates nearly Rp400 trillion ($24 billion) in bank loans and financing could be affected by recent floods in parts of Sumatra. More than 105,000 borrowers in Aceh, North Sumatra and West Sumatra have been impacted by severe flooding, much of it linked to extreme weather events.
